about: Each bill-catalog policy question has one spoken name in two fixed forms, so a stand can be said as a plain sentence: `about` is a noun phrase that reads after 'about' or 'on' ('the bill is about a higher minimum wage'); `to` is a verb phrase that reads after 'to' or 'I want to' ('I want to raise the minimum wage'). Authored to the English engine's patterns, American English; a question with no entry is not offered as a stand. Each question also has a form for each side, written by scripts/words/question-sides.ts: `for` is what a supporter wants done and `against` what an opponent will stop ("stop raising tariffs"); both read after "I want to" and "I will".
author: Claude Code, pool session
